scope: Existing staging testnet. Frozen baseline and candidate SDK assets served only to the test browser. All thirteen backend versions stayed unchanged. No deployment, activation, new resource, or package publication.
method: Sequential baseline/candidate/baseline. Three fresh NEAR-only wallets and twenty-one verified signatures per arm. The candidate uses existing session observations for signing lane discovery; prepare still provides fresh authority and quota.
decision: Keep the redundant-request removal. Repeated signing makes three Gateway requests instead of four. Authorization-probe timing isolates the removed wait; whole-signing medians also include network and confirmation variation.

e2e.command: Build the candidate SDK and local Gateway; run passkey.ed25519-yao-local.contract.test.ts with the two NEAR session-observation and changed-prepare-authority tests.

limitations: Three candidate wallets. Sequential samples do not establish a percentile or a guaranteed whole-flow saving.
sdkSigningMs spans SDK invocation through signed output and includes automated confirmation, required nonce/RPC work, and MPC. It excludes blockchain transaction submission and confirmation.
elapsedToVerifiedMs also includes browser interaction and verification overhead. Registration includes funding and provisioning. Unlock includes the unlock lifecycle.
signature_total measures prepare, client share creation and finalize. It excludes the earlier lane and session reads, so this change does not directly reduce that metric.
Request counts cover Gateway POST requests overlapping each browser workload. Registration and unlock counts can include background work.
D1 counters and Gateway-to-Console counters were unavailable. Null does not mean zero. Browser-to-Console requests were zero.
No Yao protocol, DO initialization, placement or backend change was made. Registration setup variation is not an optimization result.
Local E2Es cover quota exhaustion, page refresh, changed prepare authority, and subsequent valid signing. Export keeps the exact authorization reader.

reproduction.build: Public .artifacts/r155b-phase6q/build.py builds baseline and candidate SDKs from source.json. Unchanged WASM artifacts are shared.
reproduction.local: Public .artifacts/r155b-phase6q/test-local.py runs the two production browser lifecycle checks and saves request/authority artifacts.
reproduction.hosted: Private .artifacts/r155b-phase6q-hosted/run.py serves each frozen SDK through the existing NEAR-only browser harness, guards versions around every arm, and closes its tails in finally.
